summary.text: Zeus resolved to destroy the men of the Bronze Age beneath the waters. One chest rode the flood, carrying Deucalion and Pyrrha — and from the stones they cast over their shoulders a new human race was born.

chapters.title: The wrath of Zeus
chapters.text: When Zeus would destroy the men of the Bronze Age, he loosed the rains of heaven. In Ovid's telling the last offence was Lycaon's impious table — a king who served human flesh to a god and was turned into a wolf.

chapters.title: The chest on the waters
chapters.text: By the advice of his father Prometheus, Deucalion built a chest, stored it with provisions, and embarked with Pyrrha. Nine days and nine nights he drifted over the drowned world before grounding on the heights of Parnassus.

chapters.title: The bones of the mother
chapters.text: Bidden by the oracle to cast the bones of their mother behind them, they understood: the stones of the earth. Those Deucalion threw became men, those Pyrrha threw became women — and their son Hellen gave his name to the Hellenes.

cast.name: Pyrrha
cast.role: First woman of the new race
